source.title: Trajectory-Dependent Generalization Bounds for Pairwise Learning with φ-mixing Samples
source.authors: Liyuan Liu; Hong Chen; Wei-Fu Li; Tieliang Gong; Hao Deng; Yu-Long Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no garbling or cut-off is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments measuring how trajectory persistent-homology dimension relates to the generalization gap, a different measure aimed at the claim's relationship between trained-network properties and the gap. Its primary contribution is theoretical analysis of pairwise learning with φ-mixing samples.
record.gate_note: The results that bear on V7 are the reported PH-dimension/generalization-gap association and the stated weaker association at smaller batch sizes. Sample-size trends and architecture descriptions are not separate claim-version results. Prior-work comparisons in the introduction and related-work sections are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures trajectory persistent-homology dimension and generalization gaps in synthetic pairwise gradient learning. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, so its results do not test V7. No other claim version is tested; varying batch size without a fixed-epoch held-out-performance comparison does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish trajectory-dependent generalization bounds for pairwise learning with φ-mixing observations and report numerical results consistent with their analysis, including PH-dimension/gap associations and decreasing gaps with increasing sample size. They do not establish a result about magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments measure persistent-homology dimension rather than magnitude-aware sharpness, using synthetic pairwise gradient-learning data and fully connected networks; they do not reproduce the version's CIFAR-10/SVHN comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported PH-dimension/generalization-gap association varies with batch size: the authors describe it as strong at 64 and weaker at 24 and 48. Learning rate and batch size settings are shown in the experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 reports strong correlation between trajectory PH dimension and generalization gap at batch size 64 in a seven-layer FCN on 2756 synthetic φ-mixing samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory PH dimension correlates with generalization gap in synthetic pairwise gradient learning under some SGD settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report apparently weaker PH-dimension/gap correlation for smaller batches and suggest that noisier trajectories may require more points for accurate PH estimation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The measured association between trajectory PH dimension and generalization gap can depend on batch size and the accuracy of dimension estimation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-25)
record.problems: The reported association is qualitative, without correlation coefficients or uncertainty estimates. The paper says the smaller-batch association seems weaker; it offers a possible explanation but does not establish it. Experiments use generated data and fully connected networks, not the image datasets in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported. Figure 2 reports average generalization gaps across sample sizes and scenarios, but does not measure the relationship between trained-network properties and the gap named in V7.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on random versus natural labels.
Test-error behavior when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch held-out-performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets and interventions that remove them. The batch-size-dependent PH correlations do not measure these outcomes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.

The entire magnitude-aware sharpness claim: perturbation tolerance versus generalization gap among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and ranking performance relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Neither qualitative PH correlation supplies a verdict on V7. Figure 2's sample-size trend also fits none of the supplied versions and is already declared in rows_left_out. The introduction cites original-source work, but citation does not make the study a test of those claims.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels are not evaluated.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Batch sizes vary in the experiment, but the paper does not test large-batch held-out performance against small-batch performance under fixed epoch budgets.

The study measures persistent-homology dimension rather than magnitude-aware sharpness; it does not compare this measure with norm- or margin-based measures, and the reported association is not a test of causal direction.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: seven-layer FCN (64, 32, 16, 8, 8, 8, 4)
rows.operation_detail: Measured persistent-homology dimension and generalization gap across settings; the text reports a strong correlation for batch size 64.
rows.measure: Association between persistent-homology dimension and generalization gap
rows.note: Text describes a strong correlation for batch size 64 across the plotted learning-rate settings; no correlation coefficient is given.
rows.check: The reported strong correlation at batch size 64 accurately reflects Section 5.2, but persistent-homology dimension measures trajectory geometry, not tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations. It cannot establish V7's effect.

rows.subject: seven-layer FCN (64, 32, 16, 8, 8, 8, 4)
rows.operation_detail: Measured persistent-homology dimension and generalization gap across settings; the text reports weaker correlation for smaller batch sizes.
rows.measure: Association between persistent-homology dimension and generalization gap
rows.value: smaller batch size seems to show less correlation
rows.note: The paper characterizes the association as weaker for smaller batch sizes, without reporting correlation coefficients.
rows.check: The authors tentatively report weaker PH-dimension/gap correlation at smaller batches. This is not a partial sharpness effect and cannot qualify V7. The proposed explanation concerns noise and PH-estimation accuracy, rather than demonstrated failure of a sharpness measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
